title: Collection of excessive personal data during account registration
description: The Home Hub may request or accept more personal data than is necessary for creating an account and enrolling devices, such as detailed profile information, household composition, precise address details, or persistent identifiers unrelated to setup.
assumptions: The registration flow includes user profile and device enrollment fields beyond the minimum needed to provision the service.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Linkability of homeowner identity with enrolled device identifiers
description: During registration and enrollment, the Home Hub can associate the homeowner's account identity with camera and sensor serial numbers, MAC addresses, or other unique device identifiers, enabling linkage of multiple devices and activities to the same person or household.
assumptions: Device enrollment transmits stable device identifiers to the Home Hub.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers.

title: Inference of household characteristics from enrolled devices
description: The set of cameras and sensors being enrolled can reveal sensitive information about the home and its occupants, such as number of rooms monitored, security posture, occupancy patterns, presence of children or elderly residents, or lifestyle characteristics.
assumptions: The Home Hub or connected service can observe device types, quantities, names, and placement-related metadata during enrollment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; may map to an inference/knowledge-discovery subtree in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Identifiability of the homeowner from registration data
description: Account registration likely includes directly identifying information such as name, email address, phone number, physical address, or billing-related details, making the homeowner identifiable to the Home Hub operator or anyone accessing the flow.
assumptions: The registration flow includes one or more direct or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for direct identification from provided attributes.

title: Identifiability of the household via home and network identifiers
description: Even if explicit personal details are minimized, the combination of installation address, IP address, Wi‑Fi/network identifiers, and unique device IDs may identify a specific household.
assumptions: Enrollment captures network-level and device-level identifiers in addition to account data.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ; intended to capture indirect identification through quasi-identifiers.

title: Homeowner may be unable to prove what consented enrollment actions were performed
description: If the flow lacks clear records, the homeowner may later be unable to demonstrate which devices were enrolled, what account details were submitted, or what consents were given during setup, creating repudiation-related privacy issues.
assumptions: The system does not provide the homeowner with durable, accessible confirmation or receipts of registration and enrollment actions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for non-repudiation/accountability concerns.

title: Insufficient transparency about data use during registration and enrollment
description: The flow may not adequately inform the homeowner what personal data and device metadata are collected, for what purposes they are used, how long they are retained, and with whom they are shared.
assumptions: Notices are incomplete, overly generic, or not presented at the point of data collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for lack of awareness/transparency.

title: Enrollment data processed without valid or sufficiently specific consent
description: The Home Hub may process registration details and device metadata for secondary purposes such as analytics, profiling, or service improvement without obtaining consent that is specific, informed, and freely given where required.
assumptions: The product relies on consent or similar user choice for at least some optional processing purposes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for consent/compliance shortcomings.

title: Disclosure of registration and device-enrollment data in transit or at intake
description: Personal account details and device identifiers transmitted from the homeowner to the Home Hub could be exposed to unauthorized parties through insecure local communications, interception, verbose logging, or weak access controls on the receiving component.
assumptions: The setup flow may traverse local wireless or local network channels and may be logged by the Home Hub.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subtree id may differ; intended to capture unauthorized disclosure of content.

title: Access code input may be observed by nearby persons or local malware on the hub
description: When the guest enters a temporary access code at the Home Hub, the code itself can disclose sensitive authentication data if the keypad, touchscreen, UI events, or local input handling are observable by shoulder surfers, cameras, or malicious software on the hub. This reveals a secret associated with the guest's visit and door access.
assumptions: The Home Hub presents or processes the code entry locally and an observer or compromised component could access the entered value or related events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected as a generic information disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for credential/secret exposure may vary.

title: Temporary access code can link guest visits across sessions
description: If the Home Hub stores or reuses temporary access codes, timestamps, or associated metadata, the submitted code may act as an identifier that links multiple door-unlock attempts to the same guest or visit. This can enable correlation of presence patterns and guest activity over time.
assumptions: The hub logs or retains the temporary code or a stable token derived from it together with event metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic linkability node; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ depending on whether the linkage is via identifier, metadata, or event records.

title: Unlock attempt metadata reveals guest presence and timing
description: Even if the access code itself is protected, the flow can expose personal information through metadata such as attempt time, success/failure status, door targeted, and frequency of retries. This can reveal when a guest arrived, how long they stayed nearby, or whether they experienced difficulty gaining entry.
assumptions: The Home Hub logs or exposes authentication event metadata to operators, apps, or other components.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node chosen for disclosure via observable metadata; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Temporary access code entry enables identification of a specific guest or visit
description: A temporary access code may uniquely correspond to a particular invited guest, reservation, or household event. Processing the code at the Home Hub can therefore identify which guest is attempting entry, especially when combined with issuance records or time windows.
assumptions: Temporary codes are unique per guest, booking, or visit window and can be mapped back to a person by the household or service.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic identifiability node; exact LINDDUN Pro node for direct or indirect identification may vary.

title: Guest may be unaware of how code-entry data is collected and used
description: The guest may not understand that entering the temporary access code can result in logging, retention, monitoring, or onward sharing of authentication events and metadata. Lack of clear notice at the point of interaction reduces user awareness about privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: The Home Hub provides limited or no privacy notice during the code-entry interaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic unawareness node; exact subtree may differ depending on whether the concern is missing notice, unclear purposes, or hidden recipients.

title: Code-entry processing may exceed consent or expected purpose
description: Data from the guest's temporary access code entry may be retained or reused for purposes beyond unlocking the door, such as analytics, behavior profiling, incident investigation beyond necessity, or sharing with third-party services, without a lawful basis or adequate consent from the guest.
assumptions: The system retains and repurposes code-entry data beyond immediate authentication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro node depends on the specific compliance obligation at issue.

title: Guest can plausibly deny entering the code if evidence is incomplete or ambiguous
description: If the system does not create trustworthy, privacy-respecting evidence of the code-entry event, a guest may later deny having attempted or performed the unlock. This affects accountability around the interaction and may lead to additional intrusive monitoring to compensate.
assumptions: The system relies on weak or ambiguous records of user input and unlock attempts.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is less commonly emphasized as a privacy harm on this simple flow; included because accountability gaps can drive excessive data collection. Node id is a best-fit generic choice.

title: Sensor event history in the local log can link activities over time
description: A persistent local event log containing motion, door, and other sensor events can be used to correlate repeated events into patterns of behavior for the same household or occupants, enabling linkage of separate actions over time.
assumptions: The local event log retains timestamped events and they are associated with the same home, device set, or user context over time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via stored records; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Event log can identify occupancy and household routines
description: Even if entries are simple sensor events, the sequence and timing of motion and door events can reveal when residents are home, asleep, away, or following specific routines, effectively identifying a household's lifestyle and potentially specific individuals.
assumptions: Attackers or unauthorized local users can access the log contents, and timestamps are sufficiently precise to infer routines.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability/inference from event data; exact node label may vary.

title: Local event log discloses sensitive in-home activity patterns
description: Writing detailed motion, door, and sensor events to the local log may disclose sensitive personal information such as presence at home, sleep/wake cycles, periods of absence, and room usage if the log is accessed beyond the intended audience.
assumptions: The datastore is readable by administrators, support personnel, malware, shared-device users, or others beyond the data subject.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for information disclosure from stored event records.

title: Residents may be unaware that detailed sensor events are retained locally
description: If the Home Hub writes detailed sensor events to a local datastore without clear notice, residents or visitors may not know that their movements and door usage are being recorded and retained.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate local logging behavior, retention period, or access scope to affected people.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for lack of awareness of collection/retention; exact tree node may differ.

title: The hub may be unable to prove what event data was recorded or altered
description: If writes to the local event log are not integrity-protected or auditable, the hub operator or data subjects may be unable to later demonstrate whether a motion or door event was actually logged, omitted, or modified, undermining accountability for the recording activity.
assumptions: The log lacks tamper evidence, trusted timestamps, or other mechanisms supporting accountability and auditability.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for repudiation/accountability around event logging; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Event log content may be reused for secondary purposes beyond home automation
description: Detailed locally stored event histories may later be used for purposes such as surveillance of occupants, employee/guest monitoring, insurance assessment, or law-enforcement review that are incompatible with the original purpose of home automation and security.
assumptions: The system permits broad local access, export, or later repurposing of the log without strong purpose limitation controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for policy/consent non-compliance through secondary use; exact node may differ.

title: Retention of detailed sensor events may exceed necessity or legal expectations
description: Persistently storing fine-grained motion and door events in the local log may violate data minimization, storage limitation, transparency, or access-control obligations if more data is kept than necessary for the intended function or for longer than expected.
assumptions: There is no strict retention limit, minimization strategy, or user-configurable policy aligned with applicable privacy requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance with minimization/retention obligations; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Upload reveals highly sensitive in-home activities to cloud provider
description: Recorded camera clips uploaded from the home hub to cloud video storage may disclose occupants' identities, behaviors, routines, visitors, and interior details to the cloud service and any party able to access the stored clips.
assumptions: Cloud video storage is operated outside the direct control of the household and stored clips are accessible to provider systems or staff under some conditions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for content disclosure may vary.

title: Stored video can be disclosed through unauthorized access or overbroad internal access
description: Once clips reach cloud video storage, unauthorized external attackers, compromised accounts, or overly broad administrator/support access could expose the video contents and associated metadata.
assumptions: The datastore is network reachable directly or indirectly and is administered by personnel or services beyond the household.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact node for unauthorized access to stored data may differ in a formal threat tree.

title: Stored clips and metadata enable identification of household members and visitors
description: Video content, timestamps, device identifiers, and account associations in cloud storage can be used to identify specific individuals, households, and frequent visitors.
assumptions: Clips are associated with a user account, home location, device serial, or other customer identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability from stored personal data.

title: Multiple uploaded clips can be linked to build household activity profiles
description: Cloud storage can link clips over time via account, device, IP address, timestamps, and camera identifiers, allowing reconstruction of routines such as arrivals, departures, sleep patterns, and social interactions.
assumptions: The service stores repeated uploads from the same household under persistent identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability across records/events.

title: Retention of uploaded clips beyond user expectations increases exposure
description: Cloud video storage may retain clips, backups, thumbnails, or derived metadata longer than necessary, creating persistent privacy exposure even after users expect deletion.
assumptions: The service maintains backups, replicas, logs, or derived artifacts subject to different retention schedules.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact detectability/disclosure-related retention node may vary.

title: Homeowner may be unable to deny having uploaded a specific clip
description: Upload logs, message authentication, timestamps, and account binding may create strong evidence that the home hub uploaded a particular recording, limiting plausible deniability for the household regarding possession or transmission of that clip.
assumptions: The cloud service keeps audit trails or signed requests attributable to the user's device/account.
uncertainty_note: Applies if non-repudiation evidence is retained; exact node id is a best-effort mapping.

title: Cloud storage practices may be insufficiently transparent to users and bystanders
description: Users and recorded individuals may not understand what clips are uploaded, what metadata is derived, who can access them, how long they are kept, or whether they are used for analytics or law-enforcement response.
assumptions: Service notices are incomplete, hard to find, or do not fully explain downstream processing of uploaded clips.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness/transparency issues.

title: Uploading household video to cloud storage may violate data minimization or purpose limitation expectations
description: Sending full recorded clips to cloud storage may process more personal data than necessary for the intended service, or reuse the clips for secondary purposes such as model training, analytics, or sharing with third parties without a valid basis.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements impose necessity, purpose limitation, retention, and lawful-processing constraints.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance; exact formal subtree may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Linkability of repeated motion alerts to the same household/device
description: Repeated real-time motion alerts sent from the Home Hub to the backend may carry stable device, household, account, or network identifiers. This can allow the backend or anyone with access to transmitted records to link multiple events over time to the same home and build a timeline of occupancy-related activity.
assumptions: The flow includes a persistent hub ID, account ID, token, or other stable metadata alongside each alert.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability on data flows may vary.

title: Identifiability of residents from motion-alert metadata
description: Real-time motion alerts may include identifiers or metadata such as account references, precise address-linked device IDs, IP addresses, or timestamps that enable the backend to identify the household or infer which residents are present.
assumptions: Backend can associate received alert metadata with customer records, addresses, or other identity data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability arising from observable data on this flow.

title: Detectability of occupancy events in transit or at the receiver
description: The mere transmission and timing of a motion alert can reveal that a motion event occurred, even if payload contents are partially protected. An observer of the flow or the backend itself can detect activity in the home from message presence, timing, frequency, or size.
assumptions: Traffic characteristics or event arrival are observable to an attacker on-path or to backend operators.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to detectability; exact subtree may differ by catalog version.

title: Disclosure of sensitive personal context through motion alerts
description: A motion alert exposes sensitive information about in-home behavior, such as presence at home, movement patterns, sleep/wake routines, or absence periods. If the backend stores, processes, or makes this data accessible beyond strict need, sensitive domestic activity is disclosed.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain event timestamps and are retained or accessible at the backend.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure of information on a data flow.

title: Unawareness of backend processing of motion-event telemetry
description: Residents may be unaware that each real-time motion event is forwarded to the mobile app backend, potentially stored, correlated, or used for analytics, debugging, or service improvement. This reduces transparency about how intimate occupancy data is processed.
assumptions: Users are not clearly informed in context about transmission, retention, and secondary uses of motion alerts.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is partly a system-level/privacy-notice issue rather than solely intrinsic to this flow; node id is best effort.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive collection or retention of motion alerts
description: Forwarding detailed real-time motion alerts to the backend may exceed what is necessary for service delivery or may be retained longer than justified, creating risk of violating data minimization, purpose limitation, transparency, or retention obligations.
assumptions: Backend persists raw alert events or reuses them beyond immediate notification delivery without an appropriate legal basis or controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance; applicability depends on jurisdiction and actual retention/usage practices.

title: Notification content can be linked to household occupancy patterns
description: A motion-detected push notification sent from the backend to the homeowner can be correlated over time with the specific household and device account, enabling linkage between events and the resident's presence, routines, or travel patterns.
assumptions: The notification is associated with a persistent user account, device token, or household identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro linkage subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Notification reveals sensitive inferences about behavior at home
description: The fact that a motion event occurred, especially when delivered immediately and repeatedly, may reveal sensitive information about occupant behavior, presence at home, sleeping schedules, guests, or possible security incidents.
assumptions: Notification text or metadata indicates that motion was detected and is visible on the phone lock screen or to the recipient/device OS.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for information disclosure of event content.

title: Push notification content may be exposed to unintended viewers
description: Motion-detected notifications may appear on the phone lock screen, wearable companion devices, notification mirrors, or shared devices, allowing others nearby to observe private household activity information.
assumptions: Notifications are displayed outside the app and may be visible without unlocking the device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure through message visibility; exact subtree naming may differ.

title: Push delivery metadata may disclose user-device association
description: Routing a push notification requires identifiers such as push tokens and platform metadata that can expose or confirm the association between the homeowner, their device, and the home-monitoring service to intermediaries or platform providers.
assumptions: Standard mobile push infrastructure is used, involving a push provider that processes device tokens and message metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of communication metadata; exact node id may differ.

title: Homeowner may be unaware of who can see motion alerts
description: The homeowner may not understand that motion notifications can be shown on lock screens, wearables, shared devices, or processed by mobile platform push services, reducing transparency about how their household activity data is exposed.
assumptions: The app does not clearly explain notification visibility and downstream handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient transparency/unawareness.

title: Notification delivery may exceed the homeowner's consent or expectations
description: Sending detailed motion-detected alerts to the phone may go beyond the user's selected privacy preferences if notifications are enabled by default, are overly descriptive, or continue after consent withdrawal or configuration changes.
assumptions: User consent/preferences for notification granularity or delivery timing may be incomplete, outdated, or not enforced consistently.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with consent/preferences; exact catalog node may vary.

title: Analytics payload may enable linking of records to the same user or device over time
description: Even if the backend shares only aggregated device-usage analytics, the dataset sent to the cloud analytics vendor may contain stable identifiers, cohort keys, timestamps, or fine-grained segmentation that let the vendor link multiple submissions to the same device, account, household, or behavioral profile.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics export includes persistent or quasi-persistent identifiers, narrow cohorts, or repeated submissions over time rather than only fully anonymous one-off aggregates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether identifiers are explicit or inferred from quasi-identifiers.

title: Shared analytics may permit inference of individual device or user activity
description: A cloud analytics vendor receiving aggregated usage data may still infer information about specific individuals or small groups when aggregates are highly granular by time, geography, device model, app feature, or event type. Combining this feed with the vendor's existing datasets can strengthen inferences about behavior, habits, or demographics.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor has auxiliary data or the aggregates are sufficiently granular that singling out or strong inference becomes feasible.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for inference from disclosed data; confidence is moderate because applicability depends on aggregation level and vendor-side enrichment.

title: Aggregated analytics may still disclose sensitive information to the vendor
description: The transfer may reveal sensitive trends or attributes, such as health-related app usage patterns, location habits, vulnerable-user segments, or engagement with sensitive features, especially where the analytics concern special-category behaviors or niche populations.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics dimensions or subject matter are capable of revealing sensitive personal information, directly or indirectly.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node chosen from memory; exact node numbering may differ in the LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that backend analytics are shared with a third-party vendor
description: Users may not understand that their app activity is aggregated by the backend and then transmitted to an external analytics vendor, particularly if this sharing is buried in privacy notices or not signaled in-context. This creates a transparency and awareness gap around downstream processing.
assumptions: Assumes the sharing is not made obvious through just-in-time notices, clear settings, or concise privacy disclosures.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Sharing analytics with the vendor may exceed the stated purpose or legal basis
description: The backend's disclosure of device-usage analytics to a cloud analytics vendor may be incompatible with the original collection purpose, user expectations, or consent/legal basis, especially if the data is used for vendor-side product improvement, profiling, or cross-client benchmarking.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation, consent scope, contractual restrictions, or other compliance requirements may not fully cover this third-party analytics sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node from memory; exact numbering may vary and depends on the governing legal/control context.

title: Vendor may retain or repurpose analytics beyond expected limits
description: Once the analytics data reaches the cloud analytics vendor, it may be stored longer than necessary, combined with other customer datasets, or reused for secondary purposes. This reduces the data subject's ability to control downstream dissemination and lifecycle of the data.
assumptions: Assumes contractual and technical controls do not strictly prevent extended retention, onward use, or broader dissemination within the vendor environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/dissemination-related node chosen from memory; exact Dd subtree mapping is uncertain because LINDDUN Pro numbering can differ by catalog version.

title: Excessive video metadata disclosure to backend
description: When the backend retrieves a stored clip, the response from cloud storage may include more personal data than needed for playback, such as detailed timestamps, device identifiers, location-related camera identifiers, retention labels, or internal owner/account metadata. This increases disclosure of personal information beyond the minimum necessary for serving playback.
assumptions: Cloud storage returns object metadata together with the video object, and the backend does not strictly minimize or filter fields before further processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on generic LINDDUN Pro disclosure-by-data-content/minimization concepts; exact subnode may vary.

title: Backend can link video playback requests to a specific household or user
description: Because the backend retrieves clips on demand for a logged-in homeowner, the request and resulting transfer can be associated with a stable account, household, camera, and time pattern. This enables linking of viewing behavior and stored footage to the same data subject across sessions and devices.
assumptions: Backend has access to user/account identifiers and request logs that tie retrievals to specific clips and households.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-fit for linkability via persistent identifiers and correlated events; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Unauthorized backend-side access to highly sensitive video content
description: The backend receives full video content from storage. If access control at the process level is weak, compromised components, overprivileged services, or insiders operating the backend could access intimate footage from inside or around a home, disclosing highly sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Backend or its operators can access raw clip content during retrieval, and technical or organizational controls may be insufficient to strictly enforce least privilege.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure through unauthorized access to data in transit/processing; exact subnode uncertain without the project-specific threat tree.

title: Inference of occupancy and habits from retrieval events
description: Even if only the clip and basic identifiers are transferred, the backend can infer sensitive facts from which clips are retrieved and when, such as occupancy patterns, vacation periods, sleep routines, and visitor events. These inferences reveal private household behavior beyond the explicit content of the transfer.
assumptions: Backend logs or observes clip identifiers, timestamps, camera/source identifiers, and user request timing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for disclosure by inference/derived information; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Use of stored videos for secondary purposes beyond playback
description: Clips retrieved for homeowner playback may also be processed by the backend for analytics, service improvement, employee troubleshooting, model training, or law-enforcement response without a compatible legal basis or the user's reasonable expectation. This creates non-compliance risk around purpose limitation and lawful processing.
assumptions: The backend can retain, inspect, or repurpose retrieved video data or associated metadata beyond the immediate playback transaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with purpose limitation/lawfulness; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode uncertain.

title: Over-retention of retrieval logs and copied video content
description: The backend may cache clips, generate temporary copies, or store detailed access logs for longer than necessary. This can violate storage limitation and data minimization obligations and expands the privacy impact of any later compromise.
assumptions: Operational logging, caching, backups, or troubleshooting workflows retain retrieved clips or detailed playback-access records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for storage-limitation/retention non-compliance; exact node id may differ.
